rows.subtype: Team blames one person after a failure [Receiver]
rows.description: After a failed project, a team quietly assigns fault to the junior or the outsider. They face silence and cold glances, and their reputation suffers unfairly.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: In a stressed family, one member is blamed for tensions that really belong to the whole system. They feel unseen and often carry the family's unspoken problems.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Fixing the process, not the person [Response]
rows.description: A leader responds to failure by asking what went wrong in the system before asking who. This reduces the need for a culprit and increases honest reporting.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtopic: Mob and crowd behaviour (stampede, riot, online pile-on)
rows.description: A child in a noisy crowd at a fair or match shouts and pushes with everyone else. Crowd energy feels contagious and personal responsibility fades.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Mob and crowd behaviour (stampede, riot, online pile-on)
rows.description: A teenager adds a mocking comment to a viral post because many others are doing so. Anonymity and numbers make it feel harmless, though the target sees every word.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Mob and crowd behaviour (stampede, riot, online pile-on)
rows.description: A teenager is flooded with mocking messages after a mistake goes viral. They feel exposed, ashamed and unable to explain, and may fear leaving their room.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: fear, shame, overwhelm

rows.subtopic: Mob and crowd behaviour (stampede, riot, online pile-on)
rows.description: A young adult at a protest, match or festival feels bolder and less accountable. The sense of being one of many can free courage, but also permits acts they would never do alone.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Mob and crowd behaviour (stampede, riot, online pile-on)
rows.description: A person in a dense crowd at a religious gathering or concert is pushed by the panicking mass. Fear spreads faster than information, and the danger is the crowd's movement itself.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Mob and crowd behaviour (stampede, riot, online pile-on)
rows.subtype: Staying calm and finding an exit [Response]
rows.description: A person in a crowd notes exits, keeps their arms up and moves with the flow, not against it. Planning ahead and staying calm protects them and others around them.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Mob and crowd behaviour (stampede, riot, online pile-on)
rows.description: A young adult checks the source of a viral accusation before sharing or commenting. A pause of a few minutes often breaks the chain that turns anger into a mob.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
